analysis.title: AI Vs Everything Else Hits A Record 10-Point Gap In Five Weeks; Goldman Says Start Buying The Losers
key_insights: Goldman's Louis Miller and Faris Mourad report macro clients are rattled by the speed of the ~68bp rise in rates since end of August, not the level. Oil and rates moved together and then stopped, which unsettled clients.
The AI vs ex-AI equity spread widened to a record 10pp in 5 weeks. Goldman likes adding some non-AI exposure despite unclear geopolitics.
S&P 500 is up 14.1% YTD while Goldman's S&P ex-AI index (SPXXAI) is up 7.2%. SPXXAI peaked at 112.42 in August, slid into end of September, then bounced 2.3% off the low.
Consensus sees Q3 S&P EPS growth of 27% y/y, with AI infrastructure spending accounting for 50% of that growth (Jack Singer).

Over the trailing 30 days only TMT and Energy are positive among S&P sectors. Healthcare -3.5%, Consumer Discretionary -3.6%, Utilities -4.6%, Industrials -5.8%, Financials -7.7%, Materials -7.9%, REITs -9.8%.
Implementation 1: SPXXAI Nov 103% calls cost 0.75% (~13 vol, 25 delta), a defined-risk bet on a roughly 3% non-AI rally into November, which would retrace about half of the gap.

Midterm catalyst: Goldman's IBD team notes markets have historically sold off into midterms (median -3.5% in the prior month since 1974) and rallied after (median +6.5% over the following four months). Clients view the midterm as a clearing event for AI Power.

Implementation 2: Goldman sees a differentiated opportunity in its Consumer Experiences basket (GSXUCEXP). Experiences spending growth accelerated from 1% in Q1 2025 to 6% in Q1 2026 versus 2% for broader services. The basket has underperformed the AI benchmark by 14% and fell about 16pp relative to SPXXAI from its June 29 high.
Implementation 3: Health care is the least correlated group to AI, oil and rates, with strong positive earnings revisions, especially in commercial biotech (GSHLCOMB).

Goldman's preferred AI-related expression is Power Up America (GSENEPOW). US data-center power demand is seen reaching 108GW by 2030 (23% CAGR). The next catalyst is the October 12 FERC decision on PJM's large-load framework.
Goldman's Battery Backup Units basket (GSXABBUS) targets a global BBU market growing from $2.2BN in 2025 to $50.2BN by 2030 (87% CAGR), with Panasonic claiming 70-80% share.
In Brazil, the first-round election result has the rate-sensitive basket (GSBZRATE) pricing in a lower rates environment. EWZ traded over $8BN on Monday, more than IWM and TLT.
Systematic strategies selling volatility won in 2026: US Equity Daily Skew harvesting (GSVIDSK1) is up 8.35% YTD with a 4.34 Sharpe, and Copper Volatility Carry (GSVLLP20) is up 30.85%.

ZeroHedge's bottom line: the gap may mean-revert, but it can close from either side. In 2000 the gap closed mostly because the leaders fell. Rates may not be done rising, and the AI side is tested by every revenue report, as Thursday's OpenAI scare showed. They prefer owning the option over picking which side moves.

tension_points.bull_case: The record 10pp AI vs ex-AI gap is stretched, a lot of bad news is in the ex-AI price, and Goldman sees cheap upside via SPXXAI Nov calls, consumer experiences, health care and midterm seasonality.
tension_points.bear_case: Rates may not be done rising, the long bond still lacks buyers, and in 2000 the gap closed mostly because leaders fell, which would hit the consumer buying experiences.
tension_points.what_invalidates: Further rapid rise in rates, or a test of the AI revenue assumption such as the OpenAI scare, driving the leaders lower.
